producer_report.summary: CI's single `fmt, clippy, tests` job is split into a `gate` job (D121 fingerprint, lookup, decision), parallel `fmt` and `clippy` jobs, and a `test` job with a 6-shard matrix. A `pass` job writes the D121 marker, and a final `ci` job has `if: always()` and fails unless every check succeeded. The `ci` job also accepts the case where the gate reused an earlier pass and the checks were skipped. Every job has `timeout-minutes`, all `uses:` stay SHA-pinned, and each of fmt, clippy and test keeps the three cache layers with its own target key (`target-fmt-`, `target-clippy-`, `target-test-`). New `xtask test-shard <k> <n> [--dry-run]` (0-based) lists workspace test targets from `cargo metadata` and gives target i to shard i % n. Targets are libs, bins, integration-test files, and one doctest run per lib. A non-dry run does one `cargo test --locked -p <pkg> <selector>` per target and reports all failures. `xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs` parses ci.yml, runs `test-shard --dry-run` for each listed shard, and compares the result with an independent oracle from `cargo metadata`. The oracle is cross-checked by `src_path` against source files on disk, so athena-cli's renamed `athena` bin is handled. Negative cases cover shape mutations of ci.yml and wrong-but-well-formed shard sets fed to `check_cover`. The same file also tests the ci job's script by running it with `sh`, the job layout, SHA pinning and the caches. The two D121 tests in policy.rs now read the `gate`, `pass` and check jobs. The reused-pass log line and three doc strings now name the gate job. CHANGELOG.md and docs/design/ci-routing.md (new section 4.4) are updated. They say the new run time is not measured and is left to the throughput review, and they record three known effects.

criteria_check.criterion: Grep of .github/workflows/ci.yml shows separate jobs for fmt, clippy and a test job with `strategy.matrix` of 6 shards, plus a job with `name: ci` whose `needs` lists fmt, clippy and the test job and which uses `if: always()` and fails when any needed result is not success; every job has `timeout-minutes`.
criteria_check.evidence: ci.yml has jobs gate, fmt, clippy, test (`strategy.matrix.shard: [0..5]`), pass, ci, history, attribution and pr-head. The ci job has `name: ci`, `needs: [gate, fmt, clippy, test]` and `if: always()`. Tests workflow_jobs_are_separate_sharded_and_gated_by_ci and workflow_jobs_reject_a_missing_gate_condition_need_or_timeout pass; the second shows mutated copies (no `if: always()`, a dropped need, a stripped timeout, a renamed job) are rejected. workflow_ci_job_is_green_only_when_every_check_succeeded runs the ci job's real script with `sh`: it exits non-zero for failure, cancelled or skipped results unless the gate reused a pass. Run with `cargo test -p xtask --test ci_shards -- workflow_`.

criteria_check.criterion: All `uses:` lines in ci.yml remain pinned by 40-hex commit SHA, the three cache layers (toolchain, registry, target) and the D121 fingerprint/ci-pass lookup, gate and mark steps are still present, and the pass marker is saved only after all checks succeeded.
criteria_check.evidence: workflow_actions_are_pinned requires every `uses:` line to carry a 40-hex SHA. workflow_caches_keep_three_layers_in_each_check_job checks the three restore and save layers and the per-job target keys in fmt, clippy and test, and that shard-0-only saves are used in test. It also checks the ci-pass lookup in gate and the mark in pass. The two re-pointed policy.rs tests pass. They check that the gate runs fingerprint, lookup, decision and report in order, and that each check job needs the gate. They also check that `pass` has no job-level `if` and no always/failure/cancelled, and that its mark and save steps come after the results step. Run `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` and `cargo test -p xtask --test ci_shards -- workflow_`.

criteria_check.criterion: An xtask test reads .github/workflows/ci.yml, extracts each shard's test command and the shard count, and fails when the shards do not partition the workspace test targets exactly once; run `cargo test -p xtask` and see it pass, and a negative case inside the test (a mutated shard list with a dropped or duplicated shard) is shown to fail the check.
criteria_check.evidence: In xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs, shards_in_ci_yml_partition_every_workspace_test_target passes. partition_rejects_a_changed_shard_list rejects a dropped shard, a duplicated shard, a shard past n, a changed n, a hard-coded shard in the command, and a non-literal matrix. Each mutation is asserted to differ from the original. The cover_rejects_* tests call `check_cover` directly with well-formed but wrong shard sets, and each error names the unit: a unit in no shard, a unit in two shards, a unit twice in one shard, an extra oracle unit, and a shard unit that is not a target. `cargo test -p xtask --locked` passed in full.

criteria_check.criterion: `cargo run -p xtask -- test-shard <k> <n>` exists; for n=6 and k in 0..5 (or the documented index base) the selected targets are disjoint and their union equals the target set of `cargo test --workspace`; a test in xtask asserts this, and invalid k/n (k>=n, n=0) exits with an error. Run `cargo test -p xtask`.
criteria_check.evidence: The subcommand is dispatched in main.rs and implemented in shard.rs (0-based, documented in the module doc, usage and changelog). test_shard_6_is_disjoint_and_equals_the_workspace_target_set and test_shard_1_equals_the_workspace compare the dry-run output with the independent oracle, and oracle_matches_files_on_disk validates the oracle by file path. test_shard_rejects_bad_arguments runs `6 6`, `0 0`, `3 2`, `x 6`, one argument and none, and asserts non-zero exit and `error:` on stderr. shard.rs unit tests cover select for n = 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 9 and an n larger than the unit count, and argument parsing. All pass in `cargo test -p xtask --locked`.

open_issues: EARLY_RUN_JOB in crates/athena-core/src/gh/early.rs still names 'fmt, clippy, tests', so land's early wait will find no such check run and end at once. This is out of file scope and is recorded as a known effect in the changelog and design doc. The follow-up should name the job that writes the marker (`pass`), not `ci`, because `ci` does not wait for `pass`.
Branch protection (outside the repository) must change from `fmt, clippy, tests` to `ci`.
Every compute job still runs `./setup.sh --ci`, which builds athena in release mode. fmt and clippy may not need it. It is kept for fidelity with the old job, and the throughput review can judge.

Index-modulo sharding can leave shards unbalanced, and per-unit `cargo test -p` runs may resolve features differently from one `--workspace` run. Grouping by package or weighting by size are follow-ups after real shard times exist.

The brief's expected deliverables omit xtask/tests/policy.rs, xtask/src/ci_cache.rs and xtask/tests/fingerprint.rs. I edited them because the layout change forces it: the policy tests found the old job name, and the log line and docs named it. All sit under xtask/, which the request's Files line lists, and no assertion was weakened.
mistakes: My first policy-test run failed because a comment above the `ci` job, which mentions `if: always()`, fell inside the `pass` job's slice. I fixed it by filtering comment lines in the pass-job assertions.
I started the full `cargo test --locked` in the background and could not read its output because of the path restriction; I only saw its exit code (0) from the completion notice.
learnings: The workspace is virtual with 10 crates plus xtask. athena-cli declares `[[bin]] name = "athena"`, so its bin target name differs from the package name. The oracle and `test-shard` use the metadata target name, giving `athena-cli --bin athena`.

The Athena policy hook blocks Read and Grep on paths outside the working directory, including cargo's persisted output and background task output files. It also blocks `cp`, `tail` and `sleep`. A blocking cargo command can wait on the build-directory file lock.

policy.rs's D121 tests looked up the job by its `name:` line and sliced to `\n  history:`. Any job rename or reorder breaks them, so they now use a `job_text(id)` helper keyed on the two-space-indent job key.
GitHub Actions job `if:` comment lines between jobs fall inside the previous job's text slice, so tests that scan for words like `always()` must drop comment lines first.
desires: A way to read background task output files inside the working-directory restriction, or a foreground wait.

A YAML parser in the dependency set. ci.yml is read with line regexes tied to the file's fixed shape; moving to `include` or `fromJSON` matrices would fail the test loudly and the parser would need updating.
